_about: What a gate provider must answer, in the repository contract/gate/v3/fixture.json builds. Each case pins a different rule, not a different wording: `text` is never matched, because a provider words its own answers — only `deny` and `block` must carry some text, since a refusal with no reason is not an answer.

cases.name: an edit to a path no gate governs
cases.why: the configuration governs src/ only; everything else is the repository's own business

cases.name: an edit to a governed path that no design covers
cases.why: design before code: the governed change has no design, so the edit is refused

cases.name: an edit to a governed path an active design covers
cases.why: the design in the fixture is active and its scope covers this path

cases.name: a turn ending with governed changes and no review
cases.why: review before done: the turn leaves a governed change no review record vouches for

cases.name: a session starting
cases.why: not a refusal: the session is told the rules it is about to work under

cases.name: an edit to the declaration, which the configuration does not list
cases.why: the declaration decides who governs the repository and, at contract 2, whether CI checks anything: a provider governs it whatever the configuration lists, so no design covering it means no edit

cases.name: a range whose commits touch nothing governed
cases.why: nothing governed changed between the two commits, so there is nothing a design must cover

cases.name: a range with a governed commit that names no design
cases.why: design before code: a commit touching src/ carries no Design trailer

cases.name: a new branch: the head commit alone
cases.why: an all-zeros base is a branch with no history on the remote: only its head commit is judged. The head touches nothing governed; the undesigned commit before it is not in question, so judging the whole branch instead would wrongly deny

cases.name: a ci event that is not a range
cases.why: the ci event asks about a range; anything else is refused with a reason, never allowed

cases.name: the review scope of a staged change
cases.why: a provider that checks a review's scope names it: the staged files among those to read, the lever groups, and a kg: hash. From here on the fixture holds no commit that skipped the gate — the ci cases' tags are dropped — so every provider's history reads the same

cases.name: a commit that stages nothing governed
cases.why: nothing governed is staged, so there is nothing a design must cover

cases.name: a commit that stages a governed change and names no design
cases.why: design before code: the staged governed change carries no Design trailer

cases.name: a push of a history that held to the gate
cases.why: every reachable commit touches nothing governed, or arms the gates

cases.name: a push of a history holding a commit that skipped the gate

commit.message: feat: a governed change made without the gate

cases.why: the commit was made without meeting any gate — no design, no review — after the gates were armed; a push must not carry it off this machine
